items.lede: Today, the docket produced no substantive movement beyond what was covered in the previous briefing. Dkts.
items.body_md:
Today, the docket produced no substantive movement beyond what was covered in the previous briefing. Dkts. 50 through 55 — the three deposition notices targeting Bachar, Yaniv, and Kong, the accompanying notice of service, and the two Latham & Watkins pro hac vice motions for Michael Ardeljan and Amy Quartarolo — were all filed August 7–8 and addressed in the prior edition. No new filings have appeared on the case docket, and no press coverage has emerged beyond the 
Calcalist / CTech report from August 9, which confirmed that Judge Walrath's temporary injunction now provides Papaya with legal protection in the United States while the Chapter 15 proceedings move forward, staying collection and enforcement against U.S. assets
 — itself already covered.

The structural tension in the case remains as set out previously. 
Judge Cote ordered Papaya to pay approximately $719 million in disgorgement, as well as approximately $10.1 million in attorneys' fees and legal costs, and she rejected Skillz's request for a permanent injunction that would have prohibited Papaya from operating or required it to post corrective notices on its apps
, per __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__. Against that exposure, the fund mechanism in Tel Aviv remains the only quantified recovery pool: 
under the proposed arrangement, Papaya will place available cash into a designated fund overseen by a court-appointed official, expected to contain around $100 million during 2026, along with additional annual contributions, which could support claim payments if the U.S. ruling is ultimately enforced in Israel
, per __[World Casino Directory](https://news.worldcasinodirectory.com/papaya-gaming-files-chapter-15-after-719m-verdict-123873)__. Nothing that has moved since the prior briefing closes that gap. The next hard milestones are the objection deadline of August 27, 2026, and the recognition hearing before Judge Walrath set for September 3, 2026 at 9:30 AM (virtual).

items.body_md:
Thor CALAP LLC's no-cause diligence termination right expired yesterday, August 9, and as of this briefing no termination notice has appeared on the docket and no press report has confirmed either an exercise or a waiver. 
Thor held the right to terminate either purchase agreement over unsatisfactory diligence through August 9, five days before the court's scheduled bidding-procedures hearing.
 That deadline has now passed, which is the single most consequential fact of the weekend. The absence of a docket-filed termination is consistent with the agreements remaining operative, but it is not confirmatory: Thor may deliver such a notice directly to the debtors without an immediate court filing. What confirmation looks like remains the same as stated Friday — a debtors' statement that the purchase agreements are in effect, a termination notice on the docket, or a procedural posture at the August 14 hearing that proceeds on the assumption the stalking-horse is in place. None of those has surfaced. The status of the $52 million stalking-horse commitment is unverified.

On the docket, the new entries in the 72-hour window are Dkt. 97 (Meeting of Creditors, Chapter 11), Dkt. 98 (Objection), Dkt. 99 (Document), Dkt. 100 (Exhibit, filed August 8), and a Notice of Docketing Error carrying no assigned number. The Meeting of Creditors entry is administrative and does not move the recovery analysis. The Objection at Dkt. 98 — filed on the August 7 objection deadline — is confirmed on the docket; its filer and substantive content are not established from available docket text. Dkt. 99 and Dkt. 100 remain uncharacterized beyond their filing types. The relationship between Dkt. 100 and the Dkt. 98 objection — whether it responds to, supplements, or is independent of that objection — is unconfirmed. Taken together, Judge O'Hagan will arrive at Thursday's hearing with at least one live objection on record, an exhibit of uncertain provenance, and no docket-confirmed representation that the stalking-horse agreements remain in effect.


The Assumed Contracts and Excluded Assets schedules remain blank in both purchase agreements, and Thor retains the right to remove any assumed contract before closing; because the debtors contract through FlowX rather than directly with TNMP, the record does not yet establish which supply, scheduling, or interconnection agreements would transfer with the assets.
 
The Assigned Contracts Schedule, with proposed cure amounts, is due August 21, 2026
 — two weeks after the bidding-procedures hearing, meaning the question of what power rights actually transfer will not be answered before Judge O'Hagan rules on the sale framework. For the 11,700 wallet holders carrying $163,723,500 in unsecured IOU claims, recovery remains entirely downstream of whether bidding procedures are approved Thursday and whether a floor bid is intact to anchor the September process. 
The proposed downstream schedule calls for a September 8 qualified-bid deadline, a September 10 auction, and a September 16 sale hearing.
 None of that calendar advances without a successful August 14 outcome. The next concrete milestone is the bidding-procedures and sale hearing before Judge O'Hagan, August 14 at 11 a.m. ET.

items.body_md:
Today, the docket produced nothing substantive beyond what was covered Friday: every entry in the 72-hour window — Dkts. 149 through 158 — is administrative. Pro hac vice admissions (Dkts. 149–153), notices of appearance (Dkts. 147, 148, 154), and the BNC Certificate of Mailing (Dkt. 158) collectively signal that a widening group of counsel is entering the case, but the entries themselves carry no independent weight on recoveries, timing, or the merits.

The live substantive issue remains the lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146, filed August 7. The movant's identity, the asset or claim at stake, and the specific relief sought remain unconfirmed from a primary-source pull of the document. What is established: service has been completed per the BNC certificate at Dkt. 158, and the response clock under Bankr. S.D. Tex. practice before Judge Lopez is running. Under the standard 14-day timeline absent an agreed order, a response deadline of approximately August 21 would fall three days before the August 24 second-day hearing — making it a live candidate for that hearing's agenda either as a contested matter or by agreed resolution. The two affidavits at Dkts. 156 and 157, also August 7, are most likely evidentiary support for Dkt. 146 or the emergency motion at Dkt. 145, but that interpretation remains unconfirmed until the documents are pulled from PACER. The volume of new appearances — at least ten counsel entries in two days — is notable as a signal that parties with discrete interests (secured creditors, suppliers, or potential buyers holding contract rights) are positioning ahead of the second-day hearing, though no specific interest can be attributed to any appearance without pulling the underlying documents. 
The second-day hearing is scheduled for August 24, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. CT before Judge Lopez in Case No. 26-90737.
 At that hearing, interim first-day orders are expected to convert to final, the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors (constituted August 6, Dkt. 137) makes its first formal public appearance, and any unresolved matter on Dkts. 145 and 146 is likely to be addressed. The schedules of assets and liabilities and statements of financial affairs remain due September 23, 2026.
